notes.engaali: Owalo, the crested crane on Uganda’s flag.

guidebook.intro: Cattle, goats and chickens are at the heart of village life, and the north is home to elephants, lions and the crested crane.

tips.title: Tye: there is
body: **Tye** means “is there”: **Labwor tye?** (is there a lion?), **Lee mapol tye** (there are many animals). **Pe tye** is “there isn’t”.
Counting animals is easy, because the number simply follows the noun: **dyel aryo** (two goats), **dyang adek** (three cows).

tips.title: Many animals are names
body: Animal words are also people’s names and clan symbols: **Labwor** (lion), **Lyec** (elephant), **Ongwen** (hyena) and **Owalo** (crane).

culture.title: Cattle are wealth
body: Cattle are paid in bride wealth and counted as a family’s savings. Many families lost their herds in the war years, and rebuilding them has been part of coming home.
